success_criteria.notes: Success if the assistant checked the flight status for AA1234 on 2025-09-20 using get_flight_status and communicated the gate change (from A32 to B15) and current boarding status to the user.

task.objective: What gate is my flight leaving from? I'm at the airport now.

persona.name: James Mitchell

sample_messages: Client proposal due Friday - need impact data from the Ghana program and budget projections

messages.output_raw: Need to find my departure gate for my flight – I’m at the airport now.

steps.output_raw:
<think>The user is at the airport and needs their departure gate. I should get their flight details (flight number and date, maybe departure airport) to look it up in real time. Then I can call the get_flight_status tool once I have those details. I’ll start by asking concise, targeted questions so we can move quickly.</think>
<plan>
1. Ask the user for their flight number, flight date, and (optionally) departure airport.
2. Once provided, call get_flight_status with those details.
3. Extract the current departure gate/terminal and relay it clearly, plus any status notes.
</plan>
<action type="say">
I can look that up right now.

Please send:
- Your flight number (e.g., AA123, BA204)
- Today’s date where you are (YYYY-MM-DD)
- Departure airport code if you know it (e.g., JFK, LAX) – optional but helpful

Once I have that, I’ll tell you your current departure gate and terminal.</action>

steps.output_raw:

I’ll now call get_flight_status with just flight_number and date, then return the gate and status to the user once I see the result.</think>
<plan>
1. Call get_flight_status for AA1234 on 2025-09-20 without assuming the exact DC airport code.
2. Read the returned status, focusing on departure terminal and gate.
3. Tell the user clearly which gate and terminal to go to and mention any delays/boarding info.
</plan>

<think>I have the live flight status showing AA1234 is boarding at gate B15, terminal B. The user only asked for their departure gate and is in a hurry at the airport, so I should respond very concisely with gate, terminal, and status. No need for more tools.</think>
<plan>
1. Tell the user their current departure gate, terminal, and that the flight is boarding.
</plan>
<action type="say">
For AA1234 on 2025-09-20, departure is from:

- Terminal: B

- Status: Boarding

You should head to gate B15 in Terminal B now and watch the airport screens for any last-minute changes.</action>

messages.output_raw:
Got it, thanks  

Just to be sure I’m heading to the right place – is that out of National (DCA) or Dulles (IAD)?

steps.output_raw:
<think>The user wants to know whether AA1234 departs from DCA or IAD. The get_flight_status result I already have doesn’t include airport codes, and no other provided tool gives airport info for that flight, so I can’t reliably state which airport it is. I should be transparent about that limitation and give quick, practical ways for them to confirm while at the airport. No additional tool call will help, so I’ll just respond concisely.</think>
<plan>
1. Explain I can’t see the departure airport from the available data.
2. Tell the user exactly where to look (boarding pass, app, airport screens) to confirm DCA vs IAD.
</plan>
<action type="say">
I don’t see the specific departure airport (DCA vs IAD) in the data I have for AA1234—only the terminal and gate (Terminal B, Gate B15).

To be 100% sure right now, please check one of these:
- Your boarding pass or airline app: it will show the airport code next to the departure info (e.g., “Washington National (DCA)” or “Dulles (IAD)”).
- The departure boards in the terminal: find AA1234 and confirm the airport and gate there.
- Your booking/confirmation email: it lists the departure airport code.

Once you confirm the code, head to that airport’s Terminal B, Gate B15 and follow the signs/monitors for any last‑minute changes.</action>
